newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- FEB 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- FEB 7.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--Plans for the second floatation of Greek telecoms organisation, OTE, will probably go ahead in two stages, beginning in early summer. The share package to be floated will range from 10.0 percent to 16.5 percent. Government and OTE administration will be called on to choose one of four alternate proposals drafted by advisers in the next few days.

--The National Bank of Greece's Governor Theodoros Karatzas had a number of fairly important meetings with representatives of foreign banks during his trip to London, aimed at preparing the ground for the bank's share capital increase. The meetings aimed at ensuring the share capital increase's success with the participation of foreign banks, sources said.

--Tax inflows were close to budget forecasts in January, rising 14.02 percent over figures for the same month last year, the finance ministry reported yesterday. Deputy Finance Minister George Drys said he was optimistic that the forecast targets would be met, if developments - such as the activation of the special economic crimes task force and the implementation of computerised systems at the finance ministry - stuck to the time-frame.

--Prices on the Athens bourse marked a six-year record yesterday, with the general price index closing at 1.194,72 points, up 1.26 percent. Investor interest is focused on a range of shares, with banks and construction remaining favourites.
--Following a marathon meeting at the prime minister's office yesterday, the government gave its ultimatum to farmers: Any attempt to cut off the transport network will be dealt with decisively.
--Merchants and light industry will shut down on February 17 in a protest against the government's economic policy.

--The finance ministry will attempt to re-finance 1.1 billion dollars of the country's foreign debt as part of efforts to reduce the cost of servicing the public debt. Procedures to re-finance loans take out in 1994 and 1995 have already begun and the ministry aims to extend the measure to newer loans later, Deputy Finance Minister Nikos Christodoulakis said yesterday.

--The possibility of creating a new category of shares for the Athens bourse to be called "high risk titles" for the inability of their issuers to meet obligations to the Athens Stock Exchange was examined by the administrative board of the bourse yesterday.

--Industrial activity looks to be having a bad year so far, according to industrialists surveyed recently by IOBE. They say activity will dip. Prospects are better for the retail trade however which appears to have recovered from its mid-1996 slump.

--The problems at Olympic Airways continue to pile up, with an administrative crisis joining problems of divergence from economic targets, tense relations with the transport ministry and lack of planning. As the national carrier goes into the final year of its expansion programme, the EU continues to block the disbursement of the second tranche of a 23 billion drachma shar capital increase.
--The consumer price index is expected to dip below 7.0 percent for the month of January, according to sources. The figures will be announced by the National Statistics Service today.

--Following Moody's upgrading of Greece's credit rating, and the subsequent improvement of Greece's profile on international markets, foreign banks have been pumping capital into the capital market. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
